# Flatten golden

Byte-identical copy of `go-pflow/metamodel/testdata/bundle/cafe.flatten.json`,
generated by go-pflow's `cmd/bundle-goldens` flattening the pflow-xyz
showcase's own `cafe.bundle.json` ("Variation VI" — three independently
authored nets, `counter`/`pantry`/`staff`, composed by seven links spanning
all four link kinds) and re-encoding the result as **canonical JSON**: every
object's keys sorted alphabetically at every nesting level, array order left
exactly as produced (`Places`/`Transitions`/`Arcs` order is itself part of
what the golden pins). Canonical encoding means a byte diff reflects a
change in the flattened net and nothing else — no struct-field-order noise,
no incidental `@id` churn from the source bundle's JSON-LD envelope, since
`Flatten`'s output is a plain `metamodel.Model` and carries none.

`tests/flatten_golden.rs` flattens the same source bundle through
`pflow_compose::Bundle::flatten`, canonicalizes the result the same way (its
own `canonicalize`/`go_style_numbers` functions, sorting object keys and
rewriting a Rust-`serde_json`-formatted whole-number float like `20.0` down
to Go's `20` — the two languages' JSON encoders format an integral `f64`
differently, and that difference is not a finding about `flatten`, so the
test's own canonicalizer neutralizes it the same way go-pflow's generator's
`canonicalize` neutralizes struct-field order), and asserts the bytes are
identical. This closes `pflow-rs/ROADMAP.md` Phase 3's previously-open exit
criterion ("**No go-pflow-produced flatten golden exists yet**" — it does
now).

Skips quietly without a `pflow-xyz` checkout as a sibling of this repo (the
source `cafe.bundle.json` lives there), the same as `tests/flatten.rs`'s own
`cafe_bundle_showcase_fixture_flattens`.

The sha256 is pinned in `go-pflow.lock` at the repo root, verified offline
with `./scripts/go-pflow-goldens.sh check`. The file's own generating commit
(recorded in `go-pflow.lock`, not in this file — `cmd/bundle-goldens`
carries no `_comment` field the way the `stochastic` generators do) is
`d84dc017bfe42acd03176b74a7bb91878d72d5f1-dirty`: `cmd/bundle-goldens` itself
was a new, uncommitted file in the go-pflow working tree when this golden
was generated; the commit it was generated *against* is the one the rest of
`go-pflow.lock` already pins.
